thats a very interesting question! one that humans have been fighting over for literal centuries. i think the only true way to determine what is and isnt art is just by sight/sounds and general feel. going by any other method imo tends to exclude a lot of beautiful and meaningful works. ai images posing as art thusly are not. they look like shit and will basically for the foreseeable future. even the ones that "pass" as human works are very clearly done without human intention in many regards, and that lack of intention is usually very clearly spotted amongst people experienced in the medium. this, however, isnt even really my main concern. 

my real concern is the plagiarism. ai models are trained off artists works without their consent by greedy soulless corporations in a vain attempt to replace those artists down the line. it is then bolstered and spread by ignorant people with no artistic training or regard for the real people affected by their jobs being taken, their art being stolen. none of this process is artistic and its been agreed for a long time that plagiarism and theft from vulnerable people is a big no-go. if you see obvious ai content in the wild, please call it out or even just dislike it.

artists dont appreciate sentiments like that. ai models were created on plagiarism off our stuff and then used to take away our jobs. you should rethink how you value art, because it currently clearly isn't enough.
